light_description: Japanese handmade overdrive built around KGR Harmony's Nanbu-tekki cast-iron enclosure concept; flagship model released in 2020 after collaborative enclosure development with Oitomi in Iwate.
Current KGR Harmony distortion in the Nanbu-tekki enclosure family, documented in the builder's active Japanese store.
Current Nanbu-tekki boost design from KGR Harmony; retained as dirt-adjacent because the builder positions it as a gain-stage utility rather than a primary dirt model.
Current KGR Harmony fuzz using a Ram's Head-inspired voicing and cast-iron Nanbu-tekki enclosure.
Current KGR Harmony overdrive with a classic Japanese mid-forward drive concept, documented by the builder as part of the Nanbu-tekki pedal family.
Tokyo one-person handmade fuzz based on germanium-era Fuzz Face architecture; documented in the builder's earlier store as the foundational product lineage.
Limited first-generation octave fuzz, explicitly capped at 50 units; builder states later Fuzzman releases may return with changed appearance and circuit/component specifications.
Current Tokyo handmade fuzz evolving the builder's original muzz face / Cashew Nuts FUZZ concept while retaining its characteristic Fuzz Face-derived response.
Current flagship fuzz model in Lemon & Ginger's Tokyo handmade catalog; retained pending deeper chronology and relationship mapping.
Current high-output dirt model in the builder's flagship catalog; exact historical introduction date remains open for later chronology work.
Current handmade drive pedal in Lemon & Ginger's flagship catalog; retained as a dirt model pending deeper model-history research.
Japanese boutique Dumble-style overdrive with Level, Gain, A.M.C. and Tone controls, documented in the builder's historical catalog and later market records.
Current Japanese overdrive built around 1960s blackface amplifier voicing, with two-band EQ and three clip modes.
Japanese boutique Klone-style overdrive with expanded fat, clipping and bypass controls documented in Studio Daydream's established product range.
Japanese boutique Klone-style overdrive in the established Studio Daydream range, representing the simplified Silver configuration.
Historical Studio Daydream dual-channel overdrive documented from Okayama, Japan; based on the Landgraff Dynamic Overdrive concept with added clipping and boost controls.
Historical Japanese boutique overdrive documented in the secondary market as BJFE Honey Bee-inspired; retained as a provenance lead pending stronger first-party chronology.
Japanese handmade overdrive using the brand's distinctive machined high-purity aluminum enclosure; retailer and catalog records identify it as a core Shigemori drive model.
Compact Shigemori drive variant preserving the broader CUSTOM/DELUXE concept with a distinct gain range; treat as a related model-state, not a wholly unrelated builder product.
Evolution of RUBY STONE with a wider range and added bass control, documented as a Japanese handmade Shigemori drive.
Japanese handmade bass overdrive with a simple Volume/Tone/Gain control set and machined aluminum monoblock enclosure.
Japanese boutique overdrive from KarDiaN's Shiga workshop, developed around vintage overdrive research and a two-EQ midrange concept.
Collaborative KarDiaN overdrive developed with legendary engineer Susumu Tamura after studying multiple vintage Tube Screamer-family units; preserve the designer relationship separately.
Japanese drive pedal using a seven-diode clipping concept to produce a more compressed, grainy small-amp distortion character.
Current high-gain Japanese distortion descended from the original titania, with expanded volume, stronger mid control and a character switch.
Japanese boutique fuzz developed after analysis of a rare vintage Guild Ram's Head Big Muff, reinterpreted with transistor/FET gain stages and two-band EQ.
Japanese handmade transparent-style overdrive from builder nanase; the builder brand was launched in 2022 and Noa became its early flagship drive.
Current Petla drive model documented in the builder's official online storefront alongside Noa and Rev.
Current Petla drive/preamp model introduced after Noa and Ive; retain chronology and role relationships for later product-state mapping.
